title: Opening and Ruth's mother, the blues and Bessie Smith
summary: Introduction to the interview, her belting voice, and her mother who loved Bessie Smith and made her learn the blues.

Ruth Brisbane is a veteran stage actress and accomplished blues and jazz vocalist. Her Broadway credits include “The Wiz” and “South Pacific” and she created and starred in a one-woman show entitled “The Legacy of Bessie Smith.” Ruth appeared in the Paris production of “Black and Blue” and currently performs regularly with the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band.
Ruth was interviewed in Clinton, NY on April 2, 2013, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive. Her husband, Milt Robinson, participated briefly in the interview.
My name is Monk Rowe and we are filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive today with Ruth Brisbane. Welcome to Hamilton.
I so much enjoyed your singing today, and I was struck by — as we talked beforehand — you have a normal-sounding speaking voice, but when you sang, man, that delivery was so powerful.
Is that a conscious change for you?
I have no idea whether it’s a conscious change. I was not formally trained so I guess it’s what they’d call “belting it out.”
Yeah. I think today I mentioned that my mother sang, and she was a tiny lady but she could belt it out, yes.
What kind of songs would she have sung around the house?

Around the house she loved Bessie Smith, and the heyday of her era was the Blues Era. She was born in 1900. So in the twenties she would have been in the twenties, a young woman. She was married and had children — a brood — with my dad. And she loved the blues. In fact, when I started singing she said you’ve got to learn a blues. I didn’t know a blues from, you know swing or whatever. I was listening to people like Ella and Dinah, and well Dinah was a good blues singer, but I couldn’t differentiate blues and swing. And I wasn’t doing any blues. But my mother forced me to learn blues.
That’s very interesting. I’ve read that some African-American households thought blues was the devil’s music, or something like that.
Uh huh. Well people who are religious, yeah. They didn’t want it played and so forth. And listening to some of the old songs – they could be quite spicy.
